worked_example.problem: In the drawing of a plant cell, what is part {bioLetter(k, 6, 5)}, and what does it do?
steps: Part {bioLetter(k, 6, 5)} points to the small green bodies in the cytoplasm.
These are chloroplasts: they contain chlorophyll and make food by photosynthesis.
worked_example.answer: A chloroplast: it makes food by photosynthesis.

cards.idea: Every cell has a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a nucleus.
example: The nucleus is the control centre of the cell.

cards.idea: Plant cells also have a cell wall, a large vacuole and (in green parts) chloroplasts.
example: The cell wall makes plant cells look like little boxes.

cards.idea: Each part has a job: the membrane controls entry, the nucleus controls the cell, chloroplasts make food.
example: The vacuole full of sap keeps a leaf firm; without water, the leaf wilts.

pick.why: The cell wall is a firm outer layer that gives the plant cell its shape and support.
The cell membrane is a thin layer that controls what enters and leaves the cell.
The cytoplasm is the jelly where most of the cell’s work happens.
The nucleus controls the cell and holds the instructions for its life.
The vacuole is a large space full of cell sap that keeps the cell firm.
The chloroplast contains green chlorophyll and makes food by photosynthesis.

question.prompt: This is a plant cell. Which labelled structure forms its supporting outer layer, outside the cell membrane?
solution: The cell wall is outside the membrane and supports the cell.

question.prompt: Look at this animal cell. What is the main role of its cell membrane?
question.correct: It controls movement of substances into and out of the cell.

distractors.text: It forms a rigid cell wall.

solution: The cell membrane controls exchange with the surroundings; animal cells do not have a cell wall.

misconceptions.explain: The cell membrane controls exchange with the surroundings; animal cells do not have a cell wall.

solution: Chloroplasts in the plant cell shown carry out photosynthesis. Animal cells do not have chloroplasts.
